title.en: Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control (Transporting Lower-risk Explosives — Class Licence) Order 2025

heading.en: Citation and commencement

text.en: 1. This Order is the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control (Transporting Lower‑risk Explosives — Class Licence) Order 2025 and comes into operation on 1 July 2025.

heading.en: Definitions
Meaning of “defined incident” and other associated terms
Application

text.en:
4.—(1) This Order does not extend to an individual who is exempt by or under section 87 or 88 of the Act.
(2) The application of paragraph 5, 6, 7 or 8 to an individual is subject to section 66(1) and (2)(c) of the Act.
(3) This Order does not apply to or in relation to —
(a)any high‑risk explosive;
(b)any prohibited explosive; or
(c)any explosive that is not classified.

heading.en: Class licence for transporting own specified lower‑risk explosive

text.en:
5. Every person who —
(a)is —
(i)a holder of an explosives licence authorising the holder to carry on a regulated activity involving a specified lower‑risk explosive; or
(ii)a class licensee who is authorised by a class licence under paragraph 4 or 5 of the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control (Dealing in Certain Lower‑risk Explosives — Class Licence) Order 2025 (G.N. No. S 378/2025) to carry out a regulated activity involving a specified lower‑risk explosive; and
(b)transports by road at any time any relevant consignment of lower‑risk explosives consisting of less than 3 metric tonnes of specified lower‑risk explosives —
(i)for or in connection with any regulated activity mentioned in sub‑paragraph (a);
(ii)by using a motorcycle or motor vehicle which —
(A)is not a public passenger transport vehicle; and
(B)is not driven by an individual who is adversely affected by alcohol, a drug or an intoxicating substance;
(iii)in packaging that is and is labelled in conformity with 3.2 of the UNRTDG Volume I and 5.2.2 of the UNRTDG Volume II; and
(iv)by travelling from a place to another place wholly within Singapore —
(A)directly to its destination, taking the shortest route;
(B)as far as practicable without stopping en‑route; and
(C)without unpacking or opening in any way any of the specified lower‑risk explosives comprised in the relevant consignment while it is being conveyed,
is subject to a class licence authorising the person to transport the relevant consignment of specified lower‑risk explosives.

heading.en: Class licence for carrier transporting specified lower‑risk explosive

text.en:
6. Every person who —
(a)is a contracted carrier of —
(i)a holder of an explosives licence authorising the holder to carry on a regulated activity involving a specified lower‑risk explosive; or
(ii)a class licensee who is authorised by a class licence under paragraph 4 or 5 of the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control (Dealing in Certain Lower‑risk Explosives — Class Licence) Order 2025 to carry out a regulated activity involving a specified lower‑risk explosive; and
(b)transports by road at any time any relevant consignment of lower‑risk explosives consisting of less than 3 metric tonnes of specified lower‑risk explosives —
(i)for or in connection with any regulated activity mentioned in sub‑paragraph (a);
(ii)by using a motorcycle or motor vehicle which —
(A)is not a public passenger transport vehicle; and
(B)is not driven by an individual who is adversely affected by alcohol, a drug or an intoxicating substance;
(iii)in packaging that is and is labelled in conformity with 3.2 of the UNRTDG Volume I and 5.2.2 of the UNRTDG Volume II; and
(iv)by travelling from a place to another place wholly within Singapore —
(A)directly to its destination, taking the shortest route;
(B)as far as practicable without stopping en‑route; and
(C)without unpacking or opening in any way any of the specified lower‑risk explosives comprised in the relevant consignment while it is being conveyed,
is subject to a class licence authorising the person to transport the relevant consignment of specified lower‑risk explosives and to be in possession of a specified lower‑risk explosive when so transporting the relevant consignment of specified lower‑risk explosives.

text.en:
9. Every person who —
(a)is —
(i)a holder of an explosives licence authorising the holder to carry on a regulated activity involving a specified lower‑risk explosive; or
(ii)a class licensee who is authorised by a class licence under paragraph 4 or 5 of the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control (Dealing in Certain Lower‑risk Explosives — Class Licence) Order 2025 to carry out a regulated activity involving a specified lower‑risk explosive;
(b)transports by road outside of impermissible transport hours any relevant consignment of lower‑risk explosives consisting of 3 or more metric tonnes of specified lower‑risk explosives —
(i)for or in connection with any regulated activity mentioned in sub‑paragraph (a);
(ii)by using a goods vehicle which —
(A)is a suitable motor vehicle for that relevant consignment;
(B)is marked in accordance with SS586; and
(C)is driven by an individual who holds a HAZMAT driving licence and has successfully completed training conducted by the Singapore Civil Defence Force on the dangers of explosive precursors, the action to be taken in an emergency involving explosive precursors, and the requirements under the Fire Safety (Petroleum and Flammable Materials) Regulations with respect to the carrying of documents about lower‑risk explosives;
(iii)in packaging that is and is labelled in conformity with 3.2 of the UNRTDG Volume I and 5.2.2 of the UNRTDG Volume II; and
(iv)by travelling from a place to another place wholly within Singapore —
(A)directly to its destination, taking the shortest route that does not involve travelling in a road tunnel and that, as far as is practicable, avoids densely populated areas and the Central Business District;
(B)as far as practicable without stopping en‑route; and
(C)without unpacking or opening in any way any of the specified lower‑risk explosives comprised in the relevant consignment while it is being conveyed; and
(c)starts the Singapore journey transporting the relevant consignment of specified lower‑risk explosives mentioned in sub‑paragraph (b) only where there is established, by the class licensee or otherwise, for that journey, an emergency action plan appropriate to transporting that relevant consignment,
is subject to a class licence authorising the person to transport the relevant consignment of specified lower‑risk explosives.

heading.en: Class licence for carrier transporting more specified lower‑risk explosive

text.en:
10. Every person who —
(a)is a contracted carrier of —
(i)a holder of an explosives licence authorising the holder to carry on a regulated activity involving a specified lower‑risk explosive; or
(ii)a class licensee who is authorised by a class licence under paragraph 4 or 5 of the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control (Dealing in Certain Lower‑risk Explosives — Class Licence) Order 2025 to carry out a regulated activity involving a specified lower‑risk explosive;
(b)transports by road outside of impermissible transport hours any relevant consignment of lower‑risk explosives consisting of 3 or more metric tonnes of specified lower‑risk explosives —
(i)for or in connection with any regulated activity mentioned in sub‑paragraph (a);
(ii)by using a goods vehicle which —
(A)is a suitable motor vehicle for that relevant consignment;
(B)is marked in accordance with SS586; and
(C)is driven by an individual who holds a HAZMAT driving licence and has successfully completed training conducted by the Singapore Civil Defence Force on the dangers of explosive precursors, the action to be taken in an emergency involving explosive precursors, and the requirements under the Fire Safety (Petroleum and Flammable Materials) Regulations with respect to the carrying of documents about lower‑risk explosives;
(iii)in packaging that is and is labelled in conformity with 3.2 of the UNRTDG Volume I and 5.2.2 of the UNRTDG Volume II; and
(iv)by travelling from a place to another place wholly within Singapore —
(A)directly to its destination, taking the shortest route that does not involve travelling in a road tunnel and that, as far as is practicable, avoids densely populated areas and the Central Business District;
(B)as far as practicable without stopping en‑route; and
(C)without unpacking or opening in any way any of the specified lower‑risk explosives comprised in the relevant consignment while it is being conveyed; and
(c)starts the Singapore journey transporting the relevant consignment of specified lower‑risk explosives mentioned in sub‑paragraph (b) only where there is established, by the class licensee or otherwise, for that journey, an emergency action plan appropriate to transporting that relevant consignment,
is subject to a class licence authorising the person to transport the relevant consignment of specified lower‑risk explosives and to be in possession of a specified lower‑risk explosive when so transporting the relevant consignment of specified lower‑risk explosives.

text.en:
14. Every person who —
(a)is a contracted carrier of —
(i)a holder of an explosives licence authorising the holder to carry on a regulated activity involving a lower‑risk explosive that is not a specified lower‑risk explosive; or
(ii)a class licensee who is authorised by a class licence under paragraph 4 or 5 of the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control (Dealing in Certain Lower‑risk Explosives — Class Licence) Order 2025 to carry out a regulated activity involving a lower‑risk explosive that is not a specified lower‑risk explosive; and
(b)transports by road at any time any relevant consignment of lower‑risk explosives consisting of less than 3 metric tonnes of any lower‑risk explosive that is not a specified lower‑risk explosive —
(i)for or in connection with any regulated activity mentioned in sub‑paragraph (a);
(ii)by using a motorcycle or motor vehicle which —
(A)is not a public passenger transport vehicle;
(B)is not driven by an individual who is adversely affected by alcohol, a drug or an intoxicating substance; and
(C)has on board only a driver and any other persons authorised by the person to act as the crew of the motor vehicle;
(iii)in packaging that is and is labelled in conformity with 3.2 of the UNRTDG Volume I and 5.2.2 of the UNRTDG Volume II; and
(iv)by travelling from a place to another place wholly within Singapore —
(A)directly to its destination, taking the shortest route that does not involve travelling in a road tunnel;
(B)as far as practicable without stopping en‑route; and
(C)without unpacking or opening in any way any of the lower‑risk explosives comprised in the relevant consignment while it is being conveyed; and
(c)transports the relevant consignment of lower‑risk explosives mentioned in sub‑paragraph (b) always covered during the Singapore journey and in a way so that those explosives comprised in the relevant consignment cannot be seen from inside or outside the vehicle by any individual other than an individual involved in the packing, loading or unloading of those explosives; and
(d)does not cause or allow any other dangerous goods to be carried on board the same motor vehicle used to transport the relevant consignment of lower‑risk explosives mentioned in sub‑paragraph (b) when transporting the relevant consignment unless the dangerous goods are compatible with those lower‑risk explosives according to the safety datasheet for those explosives,
is subject to a class licence authorising the person to transport the relevant consignment of lower‑risk explosives that are not specified lower‑risk explosives, and to be in possession of a lower‑risk explosive that is not a lower‑risk explosive when so transporting the relevant consignment of lower‑risk explosives.
